# Proposed original invariant gates after node-visit semantics

This is a **source and command proposal only**. No invariant child, listing child, benchmark or timing ran. The Chair must review the selected tests, budget distinctions and host-only adapter before release.

`PLAN.json` lists 18 actual existing tests with original source locations/hashes, unchanged work/tolerances and native/actual-WASM applicability. The selection covers scalar envelope wrap/rebuild, linked gain/final samples, partition/reset/repeat/finite drain, in-place buffer aliasing, admission/allocation, packed-channel isolation and independent FIR. Three spectral alias tests retain their original nominal threshold and hot-drive diagnostic scope. No new audio implementation or test vector is proposed.

`MODULE-PRESENCE.json` records read-only byte offsets for all 18 test names, the fixture entry and `TestWriteStudioExtremaScreen` in **all four existing modules**. The source declarations are ordinary untagged package tests in the bound source inputs. Excluded AR, build-tagged stress and `.source`-only native control names are absent. No test or `-test.list` command was executed. The selected original tests and screen entry need no additional Go/WASM or Next build; the presence proof does not itself pass those tests.

Native `COMMANDS.source` contains a concrete anchored argument example for the existing module pair; `PLAN.json` groups the exact selected names by alias, partition, tail, wrap, reset, capacity and allocation scope. Every future child must use the unchanged 28-second/256 KiB supervisor, 25-second Go timeout, exclusive receipts and original fixed test literals. Native baseline and candidate use the already bound exact 6/7 overlays. The frozen GoJS fixture child hard-codes its recorder and requires PCM/counters, so it cannot run these ordinary invariant tests unchanged. Prefer a separately reviewed log-only host adapter over changing any frozen helper, runner, producer assumption or module. That adapter can reuse the same two WASM modules, pinned Node/runtime and unchanged closed filesystem/post-exit helpers, require exact test start/PASS with no skip/failure, and reject every file open or PCM write.

The existing recorder caps remain unchanged: 200,000 base frames, 800,000 high-frame upper, 16 Mi numeric words, 8 MiB binary output, 2 MiB graph objects plus the conservative 6 MiB preparation allowance. Original invariant functions do not emit those recorder counters. The Chair separately reviewed the original whole-unit work bounds: maximum 374,604 base frames/1,498,416 high-frame upper for a spectral alias function; tiny EOF/dither 213,882 base/855,528 high; gain-naive 1,000,000 high-rate calls; scalar envelope 350,000 clock/query steps. These are distinct unit workloads, not a change to recorder counters. No rates, bins, warmup, tails or assertions are shortened. Unit execution remains unreleased until exact graph/scratch array bounds and a minimal log-only adapter with native/GoJS-parent observed RSS monitoring at 1 GiB are source-reviewed. Retain 192 MiB Node heap and the 25s/28s/256KiB limits; a sampled RSS monitor is not an instantaneous memory ceiling.

The accepted semantic proof covers 135 cases and 11,327,376 bytes per side for each backend, with each stream equal to its same-backend e492 archive. It does not establish cross-target full-state identity, original invariant-gate success or performance. The steady 192 kHz deadline remains RED; candidate selection and public ABI remain unchanged. Historical failures remain retained.
